title: Signal Spotlight: Ops Check-in — Model Onboarding & Regression Triage
summary: This ops check-in condenses the last two weeks of onboarding evals and regression telemetry into a pragmatic action list. Key signal: Model A (v1.9) shows a concentrated quality delta on long-context instruction prompts after a quantization change; overall pass rate on onboarding prompt-sets fell from 92% to 84% for that cohort. We surfaced three failure clusters that map to specific prompt templates and two infra/serving configuration changes. This doc captures prioritized mitigations, owners, and quick tests to validate fixes before the next canary rollout.
highlights: Aggregate onboarding pass rate down 8 percentage points for 'long-seq' promptset bucket (May 30 -> Jun 9)
Top failure cluster (hallucinated facts in financial Q&A templates) accounts for 35% of errors on affected prompt-sets
A quantization variant rolled 2026-06-02 correlates with increased token-level perplexity for conditioned continuations
Immediate canary paused for Model A v1.9 in prod-dedicated cluster pending triage
top_failures: HF1: 'financial-qna' promptset - fact hallucination / unsupported-assertions — 35% of failing cases; median confidence score 0.41
HF2: 'code-completion-long' promptset - truncation + prompt leakage when seq_len > 2048 — 22% of failing cases; latency spike seen on batching
HF3: 'multi-step-instruction' promptset - incorrect step ordering (inferred steps inserted) — 18% of failing cases
HF4: localized hallucination on 'product-faqs' dataset after tokenizer tweak — 9% of failing cases
drift_metrics: Embedding similarity shift (anchor->candidate): median cosine 0.78 -> 0.73 for 'financial-qna' queries
Token-level perplexity median increased 12% for Model A quantized variant on validation slice
failure_clusters: Cluster A: Fact-creation pattern — templates that prepend 'According to [source]...' followed by multi-sentence summarization; output invents supporting evidence (examples attached in linked ticket)
Cluster B: Buffer-overflow truncation — prompt-engineered examples with long system + user history cause KV-cache eviction earlier than expected on 1xA10X nodes
Cluster C: Step-order hallucination — instruction sequences containing enumerated steps where the model inserts an extra preliminary step
action_items: Priya: Run focused ablation comparing float16 vs 4bit-quant rollback for Model A on 'financial-qna' slice; target result by 2026-06-15; measure pass rate + perplexity
Luca: Add assertion checks to onboarding eval runner to detect 'unsupported-assertions' pattern and flag failing examples to promptset owners; due 2026-06-14 (Jira AM-3489)
Aisha: Re-run batch-sizing simulation for long-context traffic across Dedicated pools to reproduce latency spike; report findings 2026-06-13
Danielle: Prepare canary rerun plan with traffic shadowing and fallback to v1.8; include smoke tests for truncation and step-order; scheduled 2026-06-16
rollout_recommendations: Pause further rollout of Model A v1.9 until ablation results confirm quantization impact <1% pass-rate delta
If quantization rollback restores pass rate, schedule a controlled re-quantization experiment with smaller block sizes and per-layer checks
For long-context customers, expose temporary config knob to cap effective system history (client-side config) and monitor error rate improvement
Add a promptset-level holdback in rollout policy for any promptset with >15% relative regression
quick_tests: Smoke: 200-case synthetic 'financial-qna' checklist to detect source-invention in first 50 tokens
Latency: Stress batch sizes 1,4,8 on Dedicated 1xA10X to reproduce KV-cache eviction pattern
Ordering: 50 multi-step instruction cases with explicit enumerations to detect step insertion
notes_to_self: Notes: this doc is intentionally prescriptive — avoid long forks. When triaging, prioritize reproducible signal from onboarding eval harness over noisy in-prod anecdote. Keep promptset owners looped in early; their quick rephrasing often reduces failure rate. Save candidate failing prompts in /evals/artifacts/June-2026/ for postmortem.
